To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intensity of EMAS certifications is greater in sectors with the highest impact on the environment, although the intensities vary significantly from one member state of the European Union to another.
the diffusion of EMAs in the European Union is not homogeneous between the various member states, and that the diffusion is more important in sectors with the highest environmental impact.

the diffusion of environmental certifications is not homogeneous across European member states and the intensity of environmental certification is greater in sectors that pollute more, although there are significant differences between European member states.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dissemination of environmental certification across various sectors of activities and European countries.
the diffusion of environmental certifications across sectors with varying levels of environmental impact, and the heterogeneity of this diffusion across European countries.
the diffusion of environmental certifications in Europe, depending on their impact on the environment and their dissemination across European member states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the adoption of EMAS is more intense in high polluting sectors, but this intensity differs from one member state of the European Union to another, which raises questions about the effectiveness of EMAS as a policy tool to reduce environmental impacts.

, although environmental certifications are not the only way to improve environmental performance and to reduce the environmental impact of firms, they are still a relevant instrument to achieve those objectives, especially in sectors with the highest environmental impact.

, in order to improve environmental performance, public policies should not only focus on the adoption of environmental certifications, but should rather be more focused on the improvement of the quality of those certifications.

the diffusion of environmental certifications is heterogeneous across sectors and countries and that the intensity of certifications in high polluting industries varies according to the environmental policy of the countries.
environmental certification is not only driven by the environmental impact of a given sector but also by the environmental awareness of the population of a given country.
the environmental impact of an activity is an important factor for explaining the diffusion of environmental certifications in the European Union.

the adoption of Environmental Management System standards is more likely in sectors with the highest environmental impact.
the environmental certification of high polluting industries is not a panacea to reduce the environmental impact of these industries.
the adoption of EMAS is more intensive in high polluting industries.
